title: Hou Hanshu (後漢書) 88, Xiyu Zhuan — the 166 CE embassy of 'Andun, King of Da Qin'
language_note: Classical Chinese. Hou Hanshu (Book of the Later Han) compiled by Fan Ye, 5th century CE, covering the Eastern Han period (25-220 CE); this chapter (88, Xiyu Zhuan / Chapter on the Western Regions) draws partly on the Weilüe.
date: compiled 5th century CE; records an event of 166 CE
original_text_excerpt: 至桓帝延熹九年，大秦王安敦遣使自日南徼外獻象牙、犀角、瑇瑁，始乃一通焉。
original_text_note: Verified against secondary quotation; cross-check against the authoritative Chinese Wikisource '後漢書/卷88' transcription (citation_original) during ingestion.
reference_translation: In the ninth yanxi year [166 CE], during the reign of Emperor Huan, the king of Da Qin (the Roman Empire), Andun (Marcus Aurelius Antoninus), sent envoys from beyond the frontiers through Rinan (Commandery on the central Vietnamese coast), to offer elephant tusks, rhinoceros horn, and turtle shell. This was the very first time there was [direct] communication [between the two countries]. The tribute brought was neither precious nor rare, raising suspicion that the accounts [of the 'envoys'] might be exaggerated.
translation_source: John E. Hill, '"Chapter on the Western Regions" from Hou Hanshu 88', draft annotated translation, University of Washington Silk Road Seattle project.
notes: Records what Chinese sources present as the first direct Rome-China diplomatic contact (166 CE), traditionally identified with Marcus Aurelius. 'Andun' (安敦) as a transliteration of 'Antoninus' is itself a good micro-example of cross-lingual proper-noun handling for the translation/back-translation pipeline (Pillar 1, §6).
